paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. John asked a straight question: "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" (Luke 7:19). Jesus didn't wave it off. He pointed to what was happening: "The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor." (Luke 7:22). Then He added, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me." (Luke 7:23).

So what does that teach us? Honest questions can be brought to Jesus, and He answers with what's real. He also says the whole crowd should look at who John was. "Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet." (Luke 7:26). Notice the people who had received John's baptism acknowledged God's justice, and the Pharisees and experts in the law "rejected God's purpose for themselves" (Luke 7:29-30). I think that's a warning for me too. A heart that's open hears God, and a heart that's already decided won't hear a thing.

Then comes the part that stings a little. Jesus says people found fault with John for not eating bread or drinking wine, and found fault with Him for doing both (Luke 7:33-34). Friend, some folks are never going to be pleased, and that's WHY chasing their approval is a trap! Jesus closes with, "But wisdom is vindicated by all her children." (Luke 7:35). So bake the Word into your life, keep following Him, and let what He does prove it right, because the proof is in the batch.
